sentences.zh: 果然，这甚至不是此类事件的最后一次。

sentences.en: For decades to come, crashing trains could be found at carnivals and state fairs across the country.
sentences.zh: 在接下来的几十年里，全国各地的嘉年华和州博览会上都能看到火车相撞表演。

sentences.en: And Crush itself was such a sensation that it even inspired the king of ragtime, Scott Joplin, to write a song about it.
sentences.zh: 而克拉什事件本身轰动一时，甚至激发了拉格泰姆音乐之王斯科特·乔普林创作了一首关于它的歌。

sentences.en: The Great Crush Collision March.
sentences.zh: 《伟大的克拉什碰撞进行曲》。

sentences.en: Well, that is a jolly little tune, maybe a little bit more upbeat than I was expecting from something inspired by a crash.
sentences.zh: 嗯，那是一首欢快的小曲子，比起那种由撞车事件激发的作品，这比我预期的要轻快一些。

sentences.en: Yeah, and I'm not sure if it's the way that it's being played in this case or just how our modern ears hear it.
sentences.zh: 是啊，我不确定是因为这次演奏的方式，还是我们现代人的听感如此。

sentences.en: But he did make these notes in the composition for other musicians who could play this,
sentences.zh: 但他确实在乐谱中为其他能演奏此曲的音乐家做了这些注释，

sentences.en: specifically telling them how to replicate crashing train sounds with music.
sentences.zh: 专门告诉他们如何用音乐复制火车碰撞的声音。

sentences.en: Today, the temporary town of Crush is long gone.
sentences.zh: 如今，克拉什这个临时城镇早已不复存在。

sentences.en: But trained nerds can still visit the site and read a nearby plaque, which is dedicated to the Crash at Crush.
sentences.zh: 但火车迷们仍然可以参观遗址，阅读附近的牌匾，那是专门为“克拉什碰撞”设立的。

sentences.en: Always read the plaque.
sentences.zh: 一定要读读牌匾。

sentences.en: This station is still under construction, so watch your step as you exit.
sentences.zh: 本站仍在施工中，下车时请注意脚下。

sentences.en: When you think of Rome, you probably think of famous ancient buildings and ruins like the Colosseum, the Pantheon, the Roman Forum, things like that.
sentences.zh: 当你想到罗马时，你可能会想到著名的古建筑和遗迹，比如斗兽场、万神殿、罗马广场之类的东西。

sentences.en: Right, right, of course.
sentences.zh: 对，对，当然。

sentences.en: But that's just the tip of the iceberg.
sentences.zh: 但这只是冰山一角。

sentences.en: The whole city of Rome is a treasure trove of historical artifacts and architecture.
sentences.zh: 整个罗马城都是历史文物和建筑的宝库。

sentences.en: And tourists only see some of that because so much of it is still buried below the surface.
sentences.zh: 游客只能看到其中的一部分，因为大部分仍埋在地下。

sentences.en: But all of these wonderful subterranean layers of history to be uncovered have really made it hard for urban planners who are working to expand the city's metro network.
sentences.zh: 但所有这些有待发掘的奇妙地下历史层，确实让致力于扩建城市地铁网络的城市规划者们感到头疼。

sentences.en: I mean, it really does sound like a nightmare.
sentences.zh: 我是说，这听起来确实像是一场噩梦。

sentences.en: Like as they tunnel, they must run into artifacts all the time.
sentences.zh: 就像他们在挖掘隧道时，肯定会一直碰到文物。

sentences.en: Yeah, they do, especially near the surface.
sentences.zh: 是的，确实会，尤其是在靠近地表的地方。

sentences.en: Once they get down to the depth where the lines actually run, tunneling horizontally tends to not be a big issue.
sentences.zh: 一旦他们到达线路实际运行的深度，水平挖掘通常不是什么大问题。

sentences.en: But getting down there and building out the stations and ventilation and all that other near-surface infrastructure, that's where they have real probleMs.
sentences.zh: 但要到达那里并建造车站、通风设施以及所有其他近地表基础设施，那才是他们真正遇到问题的地方。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: So how do they get around it, like all those layers of history that are near the surface?
sentences.zh: 那么他们是如何绕过这些问题的呢，比如地表附近那些历史层？

sentences.en: Often they can't.
sentences.zh: 通常他们绕不过去。

sentences.en: And these excavations almost invariably become archaeological digs.
sentences.zh: 这些挖掘工作几乎总是会变成考古发掘。

sentences.en: And in at least one case, the city abandoned a planned station entirely for preservation reasons.
sentences.zh: 至少有一次，出于保护原因，该市完全放弃了一个规划中的车站。

sentences.en: Huh.
sentences.zh: 哈。

sentences.en: And so what happens then?
sentences.zh: 那后来怎么样了？

sentences.en: Like, do you just dig somewhere else and try again?
sentences.zh: 你是说换个地方挖，再试一次吗？

sentences.en: Sometimes, yeah.
sentences.zh: 有时是这样。

sentences.en: And as a result, these, you know, otherwise seemingly straightforward infrastructure projects often turn into these decades-long endeavors.
sentences.zh: 结果就是，这些原本看似直接的基础设施项目往往变成了长达数十年的工程。

sentences.en: And they even employ specially certified construction workers who are trained to double as archaeologists to make sure that when they encounter artifacts,
sentences.zh: 他们甚至雇佣了经过专门认证的建筑工人，这些人受过培训，可以兼任考古学家，以确保当他们遇到文物时，

sentences.en: everything gets handled properly.
sentences.zh: 一切都能得到妥善处理。

sentences.en: I found some gold rings.
sentences.zh: 我发现了一些金戒指。

sentences.en: I found glasswork laminated in gold depicting a Roman god, some amphorae.
sentences.zh: 我发现了一些描绘罗马神的镀金玻璃制品，还有一些双耳细颈瓶。

sentences.en: And sometimes they encounter truly incredible things.
sentences.zh: 有时他们会遇到真正令人难以置信的东西。

sentences.en: Like, not too long ago, they found a whole building complex dating back to the 2nd century.
sentences.zh: 比如，不久前，他们发现了一个可以追溯到公元2世纪的完整建筑群。

sentences.en: And it was filled with marble floors, ornamental mosaics, painted frescoes, the works.
sentences.zh: 里面铺满了大理石地板，装饰着马赛克，还有彩绘壁画，应有尽有。

sentences.en: And most of it was surprisingly intact.
sentences.zh: 而且大部分都保存得相当完好。

sentences.en: Well, maybe they just should have turned it into a train station.
sentences.zh: 嗯，也许他们应该把它改成火车站。

sentences.en: Oh, that would have been great, yeah.
sentences.zh: 哦，那太棒了，确实。

sentences.en: So I see that you have two competing forces that are, you know, I'm fully in both camps.
sentences.zh: 所以我看到你有两种相互竞争的力量，你知道，我完全支持这两方。

sentences.en: Like, I want these archaeological digs preserved.
sentences.zh: 一方面，我希望这些考古发掘得到保护。

sentences.en: I also want, you know, functional infrastructure and metro lines.
sentences.zh: 另一方面，我也想要功能性的基础设施和地铁线路。

sentences.en: It just sounds like a headache for everyone involved.
sentences.zh: 这听起来对所有相关人员来说都是一件头疼的事。

sentences.en: Yeah, it really can be.
sentences.zh: 是的，确实如此。

sentences.en: But there's a silver lining because a lot of these sites wouldn't be excavated at all if it weren't for the city's push to expand public transit.
sentences.zh: 但也有好的一面，因为如果不是因为城市推动公共交通扩建，很多遗址根本就不会被发掘出来。

sentences.en: So in a way, historians do benefit from uncovering all kinds of stuff that might otherwise have just stayed buried indefinitely.
sentences.zh: 所以从某种程度上说，历史学家确实受益于发掘出各种可能永远埋在地下的东西。

sentences.en: And in some stations, ancient relics that they find during the construction of the stations are visible in these display cases,
sentences.zh: 在一些车站，施工过程中发现的古代遗迹被陈列在展示柜中，

sentences.en: which makes them accessible to tourists and also just kind of a neat thing for everyday commuters.
sentences.zh: 这让游客可以接触到它们，对日常通勤者来说也是一件很酷的事情。

sentences.en: Oh, that's nice.
sentences.zh: 哦，那真不错。

sentences.en: I like that, that you could go to a train station somewhere and see a little museum of what was found in that site.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢这一点，你可以去某个火车站，看到一个小型的遗址出土文物博物馆。

sentences.en: That's cool.
sentences.zh: 那太酷了。

sentences.en: As a building type, diners are striking, the long and thin with chrome accents and rounded corners.
sentences.zh: 作为一种建筑类型，餐车式餐厅非常引人注目，长而窄，带有镀铬装饰和圆角。

sentences.en: Inside their narrow spaces, there's just enough room to walk through and sit down.
sentences.zh: 在它们狭窄的空间里，刚好有足够的空间走动和坐下。

sentences.en: In a built world of taller and deeper structures made with stone and brick and steel and glass, diners are kind of strange.
sentences.zh: 在一个由石头、砖块、钢铁和玻璃建造的更高、更深的建筑世界里，餐车式餐厅显得有点奇怪。

sentences.en: But if you understand where they come from, all their curious design features suddenly make a lot more sense.
sentences.zh: 但如果你了解它们的起源，它们所有奇特的设计特征突然就变得更有道理了。

sentences.en: Diners are an evolution of dining cars, you know, the ones found on trains.
sentences.zh: 餐车式餐厅是餐车的演变，你知道的，就是火车上的那种。

sentences.en: It's not just their name and aesthetic that traces back to railways.
sentences.zh: 不仅是名字和美学可以追溯到铁路。

sentences.en: Many diners were prefabricated as modular units and specifically designed to be taken by truck or train to their final destination.
sentences.zh: 许多餐车式餐厅是作为模块化单元预制的，专门设计用于通过卡车或火车运送到最终目的地。

sentences.en: Hence the long and narrow layout.
sentences.zh: 因此才有了长而窄的布局。

sentences.en: Entrepreneur Jerry O'Mahoney is widely credited with coming up with the diner, as it is, and building the first one in 1913.
sentences.zh: 企业家杰里·奥马奥尼被广泛认为是餐车式餐厅的鼻祖，他在1913年建造了第一家。

sentences.en: His creations evolved to have that now distinctive diner look.
sentences.zh: 他的作品演变成了现在这种独特的餐车风格。

sentences.en: Long and narrow, sleek and curvy with flashy chrome accents.
sentences.zh: 长而窄，光滑且圆润，带有闪亮的镀铬装饰。

sentences.en: Many vintage prefab diners came complete with counters, stools, tile floors, even restrooMs.
sentences.zh: 许多复古的预制餐车式餐厅配有柜台、凳子、瓷砖地板，甚至洗手间。

sentences.en: And they were just transported to the destination and they got hooked up to on-site utilities.
sentences.zh: 它们被直接运送到目的地，并连接到现场的公用设施上。

sentences.en: In some cases, actual dining cars were also converted into freestanding diners.
sentences.zh: 在某些情况下，真正的餐车也被改造成了独立的餐厅。

sentences.en: And in other cases, diners are simply made to look like classic prefabs for that nostalgic appeal.
sentences.zh: 而在其他情况下，餐厅只是为了那种怀旧的吸引力而被做成经典预制件的样子。

sentences.en: Which, by the way, totally works on me.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，这对我完全奏效。

sentences.en: We'll be slowing down on approach to this station due to unusually high pedestrian activity.
sentences.zh: 由于行人活动异常频繁，我们将减速进站。

sentences.en: We appreciate your patience.
sentences.zh: 感谢您的耐心等待。

sentences.en: One of the largest fish markets in Bangkok, Thailand, is effectively bisected by a train track.
sentences.zh: 泰国曼谷最大的鱼市之一实际上被一条铁轨一分为二。

sentences.en: And so vendors flank the rail line.
sentences.zh: 所以商贩们就在铁路线两侧摆摊。

sentences.en: And the name of the place translates to Umbrella Pulldown Market.
sentences.zh: 这个地方的名字翻译过来叫“收伞市场”。

sentences.en: Okay, you're going to have to explain that name to me because that doesn't make any sense at all.
sentences.zh: 好吧，你得给我解释一下这个名字，因为它一点也说不通。

sentences.en: Right, it's a very strange name, but it refers to this very specific feature, or arguably bug, that fundamentally shapes how this market works.
sentences.zh: 对，这是一个非常奇怪的名字，但它指的是这个非常具体的特征，或者说是缺陷，它从根本上决定了这个市场的运作方式。

sentences.en: Because those vendors I mentioned, they're not just on either side of the tracks, like set back aways.
sentences.zh: 因为我提到的那些商贩，他们不仅仅是在铁轨两侧，像往后退一点那样。

sentences.en: They set up their goods right against the rails.
sentences.zh: 他们把货物直接摆在铁轨边上。

sentences.en: And so shoppers have to actually walk between the rails, where the trains go.
sentences.zh: 所以购物者实际上必须走在铁轨之间，也就是火车经过的地方。

sentences.en: The market itself is over 100 years old.
sentences.zh: 这个市场本身已经有100多年的历史了。

sentences.en: And when it was first put there in like 1905, there was no railroad track.
sentences.zh: 当它在1905年左右首次出现在那里时，还没有铁轨。

sentences.en: That came later.
sentences.zh: 那是后来才有的。

sentences.en: But even once it was cut in half by a railroad track, people just kept coming to get their fish, to get their produce.
sentences.zh: 但即使它被铁轨一分为二，人们还是不断地来买鱼、买农产品。

sentences.en: And here's a clip of how it actually unfolds in practice.
sentences.zh: 这是它实际运作情况的片段。

sentences.en: When a train approaches, alarms sound so that people know to get out of the way.
sentences.zh: 当火车驶近时，警报声响起，人们就知道要避让了。

sentences.en: And vendors quickly pull back their wares, and they lift up their awnings to, you know, make sure that they don't get hit by the train.
sentences.zh: 商贩们迅速收回货物，抬起遮阳篷，你知道的，确保它们不会被火车撞到。

sentences.en: Hence, the umbrella pull-down market.
sentences.zh: 因此得名“收伞市场”。

sentences.en: Wow, you weren't kidding.
sentences.zh: 哇，你没开玩笑。

sentences.en: Those trains are almost brushed right against the awnings.
sentences.zh: 那些火车几乎是擦着遮阳篷过去的。

sentences.en: I mean, even after they've been retracted.
sentences.zh: 我是说，即使在它们收起来之后。

sentences.en: I mean, this system, it seems like, you know, kind of awesome.
sentences.zh: 我是说，这个系统，看起来，你知道，挺厉害的。

sentences.en: Like, this is a creative way to maximize space in a crowded urban setting.
sentences.zh: 这是一种在拥挤的城市环境中最大化空间的创造性方式。

sentences.en: But it also seems incredibly dangerous.
sentences.zh: 但它看起来也极其危险。

sentences.en: Yeah, and to some extent, it is really dangerous.
sentences.zh: 是的，在某种程度上，它确实非常危险。

sentences.en: But apparently, accents are relatively few and far between.
sentences.zh: 但显然，事故相对较少，而且并不频繁。

sentences.en: And most of the time, they just involve a train hitting someone's wares that got left too close to the tracks, or a table that didn't get pulled back far enough or fast enough.
sentences.zh: 大多数时候，它们只是涉及火车撞到某人离铁轨太近的货物，或者是一张没来得及收回或收得不够快的桌子。

sentences.en: Some vendors, though, have these particularly clever solutions, like wheeled carts that are set into little tracks that they've created in the pavement,
sentences.zh: 不过，有些商贩有这些特别聪明的解决方案，比如安装在他们铺设在路面上的小轨道上的轮式推车，

sentences.en: so they can just slide them back and forth away from the rails as needed.
sentences.zh: 这样他们就可以根据需要将它们来回滑离铁轨。

sentences.en: And if you watch that moment of transition, when the train is coming, it is, for the most part, a pretty well-choreographed dance.
sentences.zh: 如果你观察那个过渡时刻，当火车来的时候，在很大程度上，这是一场编排得相当好的舞蹈。

sentences.en: I mean, still, I don't know if I would cut it that close personally, but it is clear from these videos that the vendors know what to do and when to do it, you know.
sentences.zh: 我是说，尽管如此，我不知道我个人是否会冒这个险，但从这些视频中可以清楚地看出，商贩们知道该做什么以及什么时候做，你知道的。

sentences.en: Plus, it looks like the train's going pretty slow and it honks a lot.
sentences.zh: 另外，看起来火车开得很慢，而且鸣笛声很多。

sentences.en: But still, it's just wild that they wait until the very last seconds to get their fish and then just kind of step out of the way.
sentences.zh: 但即便如此，他们等到最后一秒才去拿鱼，然后就那样闪开，真是太疯狂了。

sentences.en: You must really want that fish.
sentences.zh: 你一定真的很想吃那条鱼。

sentences.en: Yes, yes.
sentences.zh: 是的，是的。

sentences.en: Supposedly, the fish is really excellent.
sentences.zh: 据说，那里的鱼真的很棒。

sentences.en: So maybe that makes the risk worth it.
sentences.zh: 所以也许这让冒险变得值得。

sentences.en: I don't doubt it.
sentences.zh: 我不怀疑这一点。

sentences.en: In passengers, this train will be bypassing the upcoming stop as service to this location has been permanently discontinued.
sentences.zh: 各位乘客，本列车将绕过即将到来的站点，因为该站点的服务已永久停止。

sentences.en: I have another short and sweet story for all you train fans.
sentences.zh: 我还有一个简短而甜蜜的故事要讲给所有火车迷听。

sentences.en: It's about a remote line in Hokkaido, the northernmost island in Japan.
sentences.zh: 它是关于日本最北端岛屿北海道的一条偏远线路。

sentences.en: There was one rural train stop that was almost entirely unused.
sentences.zh: 有一个乡村火车站几乎完全无人使用。

sentences.en: By the early 2010s, it was down to just one single regular passenger.
sentences.zh: 到2010年代初，它只剩下一名固定的常客。

sentences.en: She was a teenager, a sophomore in high school, who rode it twice a day to and from class.
sentences.zh: 她是一名十几岁的女孩，高中二年级学生，每天往返学校两次。

sentences.en: The regional rail authorities were planning to shut the line down until her parents intervened.
sentences.zh: 地区铁路当局计划关闭这条线路，直到她的父母介入。

sentences.en: Surely, they asked, the stop could stay open just until their daughter graduated.
sentences.zh: 他们肯定地问，这个站点能不能至少开到他们女儿毕业为止。

sentences.en: They got their wish.
sentences.zh: 他们如愿以偿了。

sentences.en: The stop did close permanently, but only after she took one final ride to her high school graduation ceremony.
sentences.zh: 该站点确实永久关闭了，但那是在她最后一次乘车参加高中毕业典礼之后。

sentences.en: Schleswig-Holstein region of Germany.
sentences.zh: 德国石勒苏益格-荷尔斯泰因地区。

sentences.en: Please note that for island access, passengers will need to switch trains in order to reach their destination.
sentences.zh: 请注意，前往岛屿的乘客需要换乘火车才能到达目的地。

sentences.en: I lived in Germany as a teenager, and I've been back a number of times since then.
sentences.zh: 我十几岁时住在德国，从那以后回去过好几次。

sentences.en: So between that and the country's epic railway network, it's probably no surprise that I have a ton of train stories about Deutschland.
sentences.zh: 所以，考虑到这一点以及该国史诗般的铁路网络，我有很多关于德国的火车故事也就不足为奇了。

sentences.en: In fact, one of my favorite train lines in the entire country is this little stretch of track that connects the mainland with a tiny island called Nordströndischmoor,
sentences.zh: 事实上，我在整个国家最喜欢的火车线路之一，就是连接大陆和一个叫诺德斯特伦迪施莫尔的小岛的一小段轨道，

sentences.en: which is located off the coast in the North Sea.
sentences.zh: 它位于北海的海岸外。

sentences.en: And how tiny of an island are we talking about here?
sentences.zh: 我们说的这个岛有多小？

sentences.en: It's less than a square mile, but because its low-lying areas flood regularly, it can only really support about a few dozen residents.
sentences.zh: 它不到一平方英里，但由于其低洼地区经常被淹，它实际上只能供养几十名居民。

sentences.en: And locals refer to this situation as Landunter, or Land Under.
sentences.zh: 当地人把这种情况称为“Landunter”，即“陆地淹没”。

sentences.en: Well, I got that one, but I appreciate you translating it.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我听懂了那个词，但很感谢你的翻译。

sentences.en: Right, right.
sentences.zh: 对，对。

sentences.en: I threw you a softball there.
sentences.zh: 我刚才给你抛了个简单的球。

sentences.en: Anyway, to cope with this situation, folks live in homes on these four artificial mounds.
sentences.zh: 总之，为了应对这种情况，人们住在这些人工土丘上的房子里。

sentences.en: And these mounds are built up so that they stay above the waterline.
sentences.zh: 这些土丘被堆高，以便它们保持在水位线以上。

sentences.en: And one narrow-gauge rail is the only transit to and from the island.
sentences.zh: 而一条窄轨铁路是往返该岛的唯一交通工具。

sentences.en: And so I gather that a narrow-gauge rail is a little bit smaller than regular train tracks, but can you elaborate on that?
sentences.zh: 我了解到窄轨铁路比普通火车轨道要窄一些，你能详细说明一下吗？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So basically, a standard train line has rails that are set around five feet apart.
sentences.zh: 基本上，标准铁路线的轨道间距大约是五英尺。

sentences.en: Narrow-gauge lines generally range from just two to three feet apart.
sentences.zh: 窄轨线路的间距通常只有两到三英尺。

sentences.en: So naturally, they're cheaper and easier to make.
sentences.zh: 所以很自然地，它们的建造更便宜、更容易。

sentences.en: Wait, this is kind of a little bit of an aside, but like, if they're cheaper and easier to make, why don't you just make all rails narrower than that?
sentences.zh: 等等，这有点题外话了，但如果它们建造起来更便宜、更容易，为什么不把所有的轨道都做得比那更窄呢？

sentences.en: I mean, it seems logical, right?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这看起来很合乎逻辑，对吧？

sentences.en: But the problem is that narrow-gauge lines are less stable and not really suited to modern fast trains especially.
sentences.zh: 但问题在于，窄轨线路的稳定性较差，尤其不太适合现代高速列车。

sentences.en: So there used to actually be a lot of these in Germany, but most of them were shut down or upgraded decades ago.
sentences.zh: 所以德国过去其实有很多这样的铁路，但大多数在几十年前就已经关闭或升级了。

sentences.en: But not this one, because it serves such a small population, I gather.
sentences.zh: 但这条没有，我想是因为它服务的居民太少了。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 对，对，没错。

sentences.en: So a fun fact to give you a sense of the scale of this place, they reportedly have the smallest school in Germany with just three students.
sentences.zh: 顺便提个有趣的事实，让你了解一下这个地方的规模，据报道，他们拥有德国最小的学校，只有三名学生。

sentences.en: So really, there aren't that many people coming and going, and there's not a lot of demand for standard-sized train engines and train cars.
sentences.zh: 所以确实没有多少人进出，对标准尺寸的火车头和车厢的需求也不大。

sentences.en: Oh, so not only are the tracks smaller, like the trains themselves are like miniature.
sentences.zh: 哦，所以不仅轨道更窄，连火车本身也像微缩模型一样。

sentences.en: Oh, yes.
sentences.zh: 哦，是的。

sentences.en: And they often look a lot different.
sentences.zh: 而且它们看起来通常很不一样。

sentences.en: Here's the most normal-looking one that I've actually seen them use.
sentences.zh: 这是我见过的他们使用的看起来最正常的一辆。

sentences.en: Oh, that thing's adorable.
sentences.zh: 哦，那东西真可爱。

sentences.en: So there's this little train engine.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是那个小火车头。

sentences.en: It's pulling little open-top, like, they kind of look like cargo cars.
sentences.zh: 它拉着小小的敞篷车厢，看起来有点像货车车厢。

sentences.en: Are they hauling dirt or something?
sentences.zh: 它们是在运送泥土之类的东西吗？

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: But it's all so small and cute.
sentences.zh: 但这一切都太小、太可爱了。

sentences.en: And it's like red and green.
sentences.zh: 而且它是红绿相间的。

sentences.en: It kind of looks like, you know, the train going around Santa's workshop.
sentences.zh: 它看起来有点像，你知道，圣诞老人工作室周围跑的那种火车。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And that's just the more standard-looking one.
sentences.zh: 而且那还只是比较标准的一款。

sentences.en: Over the decades, they've used a bunch of different designs, like ones that were wind-powered, like with sails,
sentences.zh: 几十年来，他们用过很多不同的设计，比如风力驱动的，像带帆的那种，

sentences.en: and open-air ones where you just sit on a little bench and chug along.
sentences.zh: 还有露天的，你只需坐在小长凳上就能慢悠悠地前进。

sentences.en: And then there's this one that is probably my favorite.
sentences.zh: 然后还有这一款，可能是我最喜欢的。

sentences.en: Oh, wow.
sentences.zh: 哦，哇。

sentences.en: Okay, so this is just like a bike with old bike seat and pedals and everything on rails instead of wheels.
sentences.zh: 好吧，这就像一辆自行车，有旧的自行车座和踏板，所有东西都在轨道上，而不是轮子上。

sentences.en: Does that mean that everyone has a kind of, like, rail vehicle like this, that they can get, you know,
sentences.zh: 那是不是意味着每个人都有一种，像这样的轨道车辆，他们可以得到，你知道，

sentences.en: to and fro when it comes to going to the mainland in order to get supplies and stuff?
sentences.zh: 去往大陆获取物资之类的东西时往返使用？

sentences.en: Yeah, every household on the island has their own little train for exactly that reason.
sentences.zh: 是的，岛上的每户人家都有自己的小火车，正是出于这个原因。

sentences.en: But there are a few other options for getting back and forth.
sentences.zh: 但还有其他几种往返的选择。

sentences.en: When the tide is high, boats can dock.
sentences.zh: 涨潮时，船只可以靠岸。

sentences.en: And when it's low, people can actually just walk right across the mudflats if they're careful about it.
sentences.zh: 退潮时，如果小心一点，人们其实可以直接走过泥滩。

sentences.en: But at any time, because of the way the rail is raised up on this artificial ridge, they can just get back and forth by train.
sentences.zh: 但无论何时，由于轨道是架设在这条人工脊梁上的，他们随时都可以坐火车往返。

sentences.en: I mean, I'm still just kind of surprised that people can make do in places like this that flood all the time.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我仍然很惊讶人们竟然能在这种经常被淹没的地方生活。

sentences.en: Yeah, it is tricky, but they make it work.
sentences.zh: 是的，这确实很棘手，但他们设法克服了。

sentences.en: Like, islands in the North Sea mostly subsist on a combination of agriculture and tourism.
sentences.zh: 比如，北海的岛屿主要依靠农业和旅游业生存。

sentences.en: And the residents of Nordstrandichmoor, for example, raise sheep, among other things.
sentences.zh: 例如，诺德斯特兰迪希莫尔（Nordstrandichmoor）的居民除了其他事情外，还饲养绵羊。

sentences.en: And here's a clip from a guy who walked across when the water was low and interviewed a resident.
sentences.zh: 这是一个人在退潮时走过去并采访一位居民的片段。

sentences.en: And part of what I love about their exchange is that both of them have these very distinctive regional dialects.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢他们交流的一部分是，他们两人都有非常独特的地区方言。

sentences.en: And the interviewer launches right in with this very northern German greeting.
sentences.zh: 采访者直接用这种非常北德的问候语开始了对话。

sentences.en: Moin, moin.
sentences.zh: 早安，早安。

sentences.en: Moin, moin, hello.
sentences.zh: Moin, moin，你好。

sentences.en: And one of the things he just mentioned is how he works both as a farmer,
sentences.zh: 他刚才提到的其中一件事是他既是一名农民，

sentences.en: but also has a side job of working on coastal protection.
sentences.zh: 同时还有一份从事海岸保护的副业。

sentences.en: Because in places like this, sea level rise is taking its toll.
sentences.zh: 因为在这样的地方，海平面上升正在造成损失。

sentences.en: So they're experimenting with different solutions.
sentences.zh: 所以他们正在尝试不同的解决方案。

sentences.en: And in extreme cases, they might even have to take entire buildings down and then raise up the mounds under them and then rebuild on top of that.
sentences.zh: 在极端情况下，他们甚至可能不得不拆除整栋建筑，然后抬高下面的土丘，再在上面重建。

sentences.en: But some families have lived here for generations.
sentences.zh: 但有些家庭已经在这里生活了好几代人。

sentences.en: They're really keen on sorting something out so that they can stay on their ancestral land, right?
sentences.zh: 他们非常渴望解决这个问题，以便能留在祖辈的土地上，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 对，对。

sentences.en: I mean, it does sound tough.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这听起来确实很艰难。

sentences.en: I mean, it also sounds kind of amazing what they've been able to do living out on this island.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们能在岛上生活所做的一切也听起来很了不起。

sentences.en: You know, and they get to own a train.
sentences.zh: 你知道，而且他们还能拥有一列火车。

sentences.en: Right?
sentences.zh: 对吧？

sentences.en: Who doesn't want to own their own train?
sentences.zh: 谁不想拥有自己的火车呢？

sentences.en: Now, before we leave the North Sea, I do want to switch tracks for just one more minute.
sentences.zh: 现在，在离开北海之前，我想再换个话题谈一分钟。

sentences.en: Because there's this one particularly famous island a bit farther north.
sentences.zh: 因为在更北边一点有一个特别著名的岛屿。

sentences.en: And it's also connected to the mainland by train.
sentences.zh: 它也通过火车与大陆相连。

sentences.en: But that's not actually what I'm going to talk about.
sentences.zh: 但那其实不是我要谈的内容。

sentences.en: I first learned about this place in the early 90s when I was a student in Germany from my first German cassette tape, which was written by the punk band Die Erste.
sentences.zh: 我第一次听说这个地方是在90年代初，当时我是一名在德国的学生，是从我的第一盘德语磁带里听到的，那是由朋克乐队Die Erste写的。

sentences.en: And this particular song, Westerland, is about a fancy resort town on this bigger and posher and frankly much more well-known North Sea island.
sentences.zh: 而这首特别的歌《Westerland》，是关于这个更大、更时髦、坦率地说更出名的北海岛屿上的一个高档度假小镇。

sentences.en: So basically, it's a parody of these bougie resort goers.
sentences.zh: 所以基本上，这是对那些附庸风雅的度假者的讽刺。

sentences.en: He's singing about how he's stuck in Berlin, and so he's sitting on a hand towel by a lake, just wishing and imagining he could be back on Westerland instead,
sentences.zh: 他唱着他被困在柏林，所以他坐在湖边的手巾上，只是希望并想象他能回到Westerland，

sentences.en: sitting along a nice sandy beach on the North Sea.
sentences.zh: 坐在北海边漂亮的沙滩上。

sentences.en: Today will be the island nation of Japan.
sentences.zh: 今天将是岛国日本。

sentences.en: Please pay attention to the rail workers pointing and calling as you exit the train.
sentences.zh: 请注意铁路工人在离开火车时指点和呼唤的动作。

sentences.en: I'm back with Kurt Kolstad talking about trains.
sentences.zh: 我又和Kurt Kolstad一起谈论火车了。

sentences.en: Oh, yes.
sentences.zh: 哦，是的。

sentences.en: And it would be, of course, criminal to do an episode about trains and not mention Japan, with its really rich history of being super innovative when it comes to railways.
sentences.zh: 当然，如果做一期关于火车的节目而不提到日本，那简直是犯罪，日本在铁路方面有着非常丰富的创新历史。

sentences.en: For example, they have seismometers that signal trains to stop when an earthquake is starting.
sentences.zh: 例如，他们有地震仪，可以在地震开始时发出信号让火车停下来。

sentences.en: And as a result, they have basically no train accidents related to earthquakes anymore.
sentences.zh: 结果，他们基本上不再有与地震相关的火车事故了。

sentences.en: I mean, in a country famous for earthquakes, that seems like a vital development.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，在一个以地震闻名的国家，这似乎是一项至关重要的发展。

sentences.en: Oh, yeah, definitely.
sentences.zh: 哦，是的，绝对是。

sentences.en: And Japan also just launched a bus slash train hybrid that has wheels for both roads and rails and converts in just 15 seconds.
sentences.zh: 而且日本刚刚推出了一种公交/火车混合动力车，它有可以在公路和轨道上行驶的轮子，只需15秒就能转换。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: Oh, I love it.
sentences.zh: 哦，我喜欢它。

sentences.en: Like all the best of public transit rolled into one.
sentences.zh: 就像把公共交通的所有优点集于一身。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's great.
sentences.zh: 是的，太棒了。

sentences.en: Sweet.
sentences.zh: 太赞了。

sentences.en: But the main innovation I want to talk about briefly is this system called Point and Call, which is not really about how trains themselves are designed,
sentences.zh: 但我想要简要谈论的主要创新是这个被称为“指差确认”的系统，它并不是关于火车本身是如何设计的，

sentences.en: but about how railway employees keep them running.
sentences.zh: 而是关于铁路员工如何保持它们运行的。

sentences.en: And here's a clip showing how this works in practice.
sentences.zh: 这是一个展示它在实践中如何运作的片段。

sentences.en: Okay, so there are these loud announcements, which, of course, I cannot understand.
sentences.zh: 好吧，所以有这些大声的广播，当然，我听不懂。

sentences.en: But what really jumped out at me is how much the rail employees are kind of gesticulating.
sentences.zh: 但真正让我惊讶的是铁路员工的手势动作有多多。

sentences.en: You know, like it's very dramatic.
sentences.zh: 你知道，就像非常戏剧化一样。

sentences.en: I take it this is the point of the point and call system.
sentences.zh: 我想这就是指差确认系统的重点所在。

sentences.en: But what's the actual point of what they're pointing at?
sentences.zh: 但他们指的东西到底有什么意义呢？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So in short, the point and call method is meant to improve safety on rail lines.
sentences.zh: 简而言之，指差确认方法旨在提高铁路线上的安全性。

sentences.en: Japan did extensive behavioral research to come up with this system.
sentences.zh: 日本进行了广泛的行为研究才提出了这个系统。

sentences.en: Through testing, they concluded that if their workers associate a habit with more than one sense, for example,
sentences.zh: 通过测试，他们得出结论，如果他们的员工将一种习惯与多种感官联系起来，例如，

sentences.en: if they're physically pointing at a thing while talking about the action that they're performing related to that thing, it can reduce workplace errors dramatically.
sentences.zh: 如果他们在谈论与某物相关的操作时身体上指向该物体，可以显著减少工作中的错误。

sentences.en: Okay, so the workers stationed alongside the train point and call out that it's all clear, like no one's caught in a door.
sentences.zh: 好吧，所以驻扎在火车旁边的工人会指着并呼喊一切正常，比如没有人被门夹住。

sentences.en: And then the conductor points forward before starting that.
sentences.zh: 然后列车员在启动前会向前指。

sentences.en: That's a sort of like whole theatrical system of making this operation safer.
sentences.zh: 这是一种让操作更安全的戏剧化系统。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 是的，完全正确。

sentences.en: And it's not just directions.
sentences.zh: 而且不仅仅是方向。

sentences.en: They also point at buttons and gauges and signs and other stuff.
sentences.zh: 他们还会指着按钮、仪表、标志和其他东西。

sentences.en: And each of these actions is designed to help everybody who's working on the rail system be more alert and stay on task.
sentences.zh: 而这些动作中的每一个都是为了帮助铁路系统上的每个人更加警觉并专注于任务。

sentences.en: I mean, if this works so well, is it found anywhere else besides Japan if other countries adopted this system?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，如果这效果这么好，除了日本之外，还有其他国家采用这个系统吗？

sentences.en: You know, it really hasn't taken off in other countries as much as I would have thought, given how successful it has been in Japan.
sentences.zh: 你知道，考虑到它在日本取得的成功，它在其他国家并没有像我预期的那样流行起来。

sentences.en: And it's not totally clear why.
sentences.zh: 而且原因并不完全清楚。

sentences.en: But there are places that do use parts of the point and call approach.
sentences.zh: 但有些地方确实使用了指差确认方法的一部分。

sentences.en: Like, do they just point or they just call?
sentences.zh: 比如，他们是只指还是只喊？

sentences.en: What do they do?
sentences.zh: 他们是怎么做的？

sentences.en: Well, for example, in New York City, Metro Transit Authority conductors have to point at a sign before leaving a station.
sentences.zh: 嗯，例如，在纽约市，大都会运输署（MTA）的列车员在离开车站前必须指向一个标志。

sentences.en: But they don't have to, like, shout an announcement along with that.
sentences.zh: 但他们不需要像那样大声喊出公告。

sentences.en: Huh.
sentences.zh: 哈。

sentences.en: I mean, is it because they feel self-conscious or something about the shouting part?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，是因为他们对大喊大叫的部分感到难为情吗？

sentences.en: It strikes me as odd.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这很奇怪。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think maybe that's it.
sentences.zh: 是的，我想也许就是这样。

sentences.en: And, like, maybe that's why they just stick to pointing.
sentences.zh: 而且，也许这就是他们只坚持指向的原因。

sentences.en: But in any case,
sentences.zh: 但无论如何，

sentences.en: there's this pretty goofy video online of a bunch of people who decided to make some MTA agents smile by putting up signs in front of the sign that they're supposed to point at with phrases like,
sentences.zh: 网上有一个相当滑稽的视频，一群人决定通过在他们应该指向的标志前贴上标语来让MTA员工微笑，标语上写着，

sentences.en: point here if you're dead sexy.
sentences.zh: 如果你性感就指这里。

sentences.en: And, of course, operators have no choice.
sentences.zh: 当然，操作员别无选择。

sentences.en: They have to point.
sentences.zh: 他们必须指。

sentences.en: Well, that's some pretty wholesome infrastructure fun.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这真是一些相当健康的基建乐趣。

sentences.en: Right, right.
sentences.zh: 对，对。

sentences.en: Especially for New Yorkers.
sentences.zh: 特别是对纽约人来说。

sentences.en: I feel like that's really nice.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这真的很好。

sentences.en: Oh, I like it.
sentences.zh: 哦，我喜欢它。

sentences.en: Oh, cool.
sentences.zh: 哦，酷。

sentences.en: Well, I'll look for the pointing next time I'm on a train.
sentences.zh: 好吧，下次我坐火车时会留意那个指向动作。

sentences.en: That's pretty cool.
sentences.zh: 那太酷了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.zh: Chris Berube是我们的亲切列车员。

sentences.zh: 团队的其他成员包括Vivian Lay、Emmett Fitzgerald、Jason DeLeon、Christopher Johnson、Lash Madon、Joe Rosenberg。

sentences.zh: 索菲亚·克拉茨克。

sentences.zh: 现在总部位于北边六个街区的Pandora大楼。

sentences.zh: 在美丽的加利福尼亚州奥克兰市中心。

sentences.zh: 你可以在Facebook上找到该节目并参与讨论。
